title: Two-term scalar quotient resolutions after flat sheaf extension
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $A$ a commutative integral domain, $A_{\mathcal C}$ its constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and $R$ a commutative sheaf of $A_{\mathcal C}$-algebras which is flat as an $A_{\mathcal C}$-module [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. For each $0\ne a\in A$, multiplication by $a$ on $R$ is injective. The complex $[R\xrightarrow{a}R]$ in cohomological degrees $-1,0$, augmented to $R/aR$ in degree zero, is a K-flat resolution [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Also $R[0]$ is K-flat. Hence derived tensor [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] with $R/aR$ can be computed using that displayed two-term complex.

source.place: Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor) and Tag 06YQ (lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat); explicit flat scalar extension of the nonzero-scalar quotient resolution

proof.text: Fix $a\ne0$. Since $A$ is an integral domain, $ax=ay$ implies $a(x-y)=0$ and hence $x=y$. Multiplication by $a$ is therefore a monomorphism of constant $A$-module presheaves. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-r-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact], evaluation computes presheaf kernels and module sheafification is exact. Sheafify this monomorphism over the constant ring presheaf $A$: by [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] its source and target are $A_{\mathcal C}$, and its map is multiplication by the constant scalar $a$. Thus $a:A_{\mathcal C}\to A_{\mathcal C}$ is a monomorphism. This uses exact sheafification, without any assumption that the site has enough points.

source.place: Tag 03EI (lemma-sheafification-exact), applied to the constant presheaf of rings; compare Tag 093J (lemma-constant-exact)

proof.text: By [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], the given flatness of $R$ means precisely that $-\otimes_{A_{\mathcal C}}R$ is exact, so it preserves the kernel sequence $0\to A_{\mathcal C}\xrightarrow{a}A_{\mathcal C}$ from Step 1. The sheaf tensor product of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] identifies $A_{\mathcal C}\otimes_{A_{\mathcal C}}R$ with $R$: sectionwise the map is $b\otimes r\mapsto br$, with inverse $r\mapsto1\otimes r$, and these maps respect restrictions and hence sheafify. Under this identification $a\otimes1$ sends $r$ to $ar$. Thus $a:R\to R$ is monic. Kernels of module sheaves are sectionwise by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so this is injectivity on sections as well.

source.place: Tag 03ER (definition-flat), sheaf clause; Section Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product); Tag 03DA (lemma-abelian)

proof.text: Let $C^{-1}=R$, $C^0=R$, $d^{-1}=a$, and all other terms and differentials be zero. Let $q:R\to R/aR$ be the sheaf cokernel of $a$. Cokernels are sheafifications of sectionwise cokernels by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so this is the quotient sheaf meant by $R/aR$. The augmentation $\epsilon:C\to(R/aR)[0]$ has $\epsilon^0=q$ and zero components elsewhere; $qa=0$ gives its cochain-map equation. By [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules], $H^{-1}(C)=\ker(a)=0$ by Step 2, $H^0(C)=\operatorname{coker}(a)=R/aR$, and $H^i(C)=0$ for $i\ne-1,0$. The map $H^0(\epsilon)$ is precisely the cokernel identification, and all other cohomology maps are isomorphisms between zero sheaves. Hence $\epsilon$ is a quasi-isomorphism by [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules].

source.place: Tag 0115 (definition-quasi-isomorphism-cochain), with the preceding formula for cohomology; quotient sheaf from Modules on Sites Tag 03DA

proof.text: Over the coefficient sheaf $R$ itself, both nonzero terms of $C$ are flat, independently of the original flatness over $A_{\mathcal C}$. Indeed, [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] gives $M\otimes_RR\cong M$ by $m\otimes r\mapsto rm$ with inverse $m\mapsto m\otimes1$, sectionwise and then after sheafification; consequently tensoring with $R$ is exact. Tensoring with the zero sheaf is the zero functor, also exact. By [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], this proves flatness of every term of $C$ and of $R[0]$ as $R$-module sheaves.

The complexes $C$ and $R[0]$ both vanish in degrees strictly greater than zero, and every term is flat over $R$ by Step 4. Apply [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] to the ringed site $(\mathcal C,R)$, with upper bound $b=0$, separately to each complex. Both are K-flat over $R$. Combining the K-flatness of $C$ with the actual augmentation quasi-isomorphism from Step 3 gives a K-flat resolution of $(R/aR)[0]$, exactly as defined by [def-pc-kflat-complex].

source.place: Tag 06YQ (lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat); definition of a K-flat resolution

proof.text: The statement [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] says that derived tensor is computed by replacing one factor by a K-flat resolution (take the identity morphism of the small ringed site $(\mathcal C,R)$ for its ambient ringed-topos data). Use the resolution $\epsilon$ of Step 5 for the quotient factor. Thus for any $R$-module complex $M^\bullet$, $M^\bullet\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}(R/aR)$ is represented by $\operatorname{Tot}(M^\bullet\otimes_R C)$. This is precisely computation by the displayed two-term complex, and proves the final assertion.

lean.statement: theorem flat_scalar_cyclic_resolution [IsDomain A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{r} (scalarCyclicRing R))] (hflat : IsFlatOnSite (J := J) (R := scalarCyclicBase J A) ((restrictScalars ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{r} RingCat.{r})).map α)).obj (unit (scalarCyclicRing R)))) (a : A) (ha : a ≠ 0) : Mono (scalarCyclicMultiplication R α a) ∧ ∃ ε : scalarCyclicComplex R α a ⟶ (CochainComplex.singleFunctor _ 0).obj (scalarCyclicQuotient R α a), CochainComplex.mappingCone.inr ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor _ 0).map (scalarCyclicMultiplication R α a)) ≫ ε = (CochainComplex.singleFunctor _ 0).map (cokernel.π (scalarCyclicMultiplication R α a)) ∧ CochainComplex.IsKFlatResolutionIndependentCoefficients ε ∧ CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor _ 0).obj (unit (scalarCyclicRing R))) ∧ ∀ M : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{r} (scalarCyclicRing R)) ℤ, Nonempty ((siteDerivedTensorIndependentCoefficients J R).obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj M, DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor _ 0).obj (scalarCyclicQuotient R α a))) ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj (CochainComplex.mapBifunctor M (scalarCyclicComplex R α a) (curriedTensor _)))
lean.note: The auxiliary abbreviations reuse the recorded constant sheaf and module category. The scalar map is constructed from the sheafification adjunction, the displayed complex is its degree-zero mapping cone, and the quotient is its sheaf cokernel. The augmentation is specified by the cokernel projection, and the final clause uses the existing independent-coefficient derived tensor.
